definition: In large language models (LLMs), a glitch token is token that causes unexpected or "glitchy" outputs when used in a prompt.
details: Such output may include the model misunderstanding meanings of words, refusing to respond or generating repetitive or unrelated text. Prompts that cause this behaviour may look completely normal.
story: Imagine learning a language by reading every book in the library and noticing, over time, which words travel together. It does not memorize a rulebook; it absorbs a library. The machine learns language the way you did — by hearing so much of it that the patterns sink in. It is fluency built from pattern, not from memorized rules. That pattern-earned fluency is Glitch token.
